purpose: The upstream each pinned corpus came from, so `npm run drift` (tools/drift.ts) can answer 'has the upstream of this pin moved since it was pinned, and did the pinned bytes move with it?'. Built by hand from every row of fixtures/provenance.md and from the corpus directories walker/scopes.json names; kept by hand. fixtures/provenance.md stays the record of WHAT was pinned and why; this file carries only the liveness relation.

role.current: This pin is what the repository treats as the corpus today. Checked on every run, and its outcome decides the exit code.
role.historical: Kept for a finding rather than as the current corpus. Reported as `not_checked`, never counted as current, and never fetched — a superseded pin cannot drift, because nothing claims it is the tip.

outcomes.current: git: the ref's tip equals pinned_commit. http: the GET body's sha256 equals the pin. ietf-draft: no higher revision exists at the IETF archive.
outcomes.moved_untouched: git only: the tip moved but every pinned path is byte-unchanged at the tip. The corpus is still an accurate snapshot of those paths.
outcomes.moved_changed: git only: at least one pinned path differs at the tip. Every differing path is listed with its old and new blob id and the new sha256.
outcomes.changed: http only: the body's sha256 differs from the pin. Both digests are printed.
outcomes.superseded: ietf-draft only: a higher revision exists at the archive; the run names it.
outcomes.unreachable: The check could not be made — network, ref or clone failure, with the error text. Never silently a pass.
outcomes.not_checked: role: historical. Printed on its own row, never counted as current.
outcomes.no_entry: The tool was asked about a corpus directory that has no entry in this file at all. Never produced by a run over `upstreams` (every entry is by definition an entry); produced when a corpus directory is named with --corpus and nothing here claims it, so the failure mode has a name in the output as well as in test/upstream-coverage.test.ts. Counted as a failure: a corpus nothing watches has not passed a freshness check, it was never given one.

how_to_read.path_check: Each entry in a git entry's `paths` may carry `check`: `fail` (the default, and what a path without the attribute means) makes a difference at the tip `moved_changed` and fails the run, while `note` reports the difference in the row's detail line as `noted: <path> <old blob> -> <new blob>` and in `noted_paths` without failing on it -- for a path pinned for provenance rather than as graded data, such as an author's own manifest lock that moves whenever they touch any file in the corpus directory.
how_to_read.blob_ids_not_worktree_bytes: Every git comparison reads the object store — `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>` for the id, `git cat-file blob <id>` for the bytes — and never a checked-out file. core.autocrlf is true on the machine this repository is developed on, so a worktree comparison would report a change on every text file on every run (fixtures/provenance.md line 398). The tool's clones also set core.autocrlf=false; that is belt and braces, not the mechanism.
how_to_read.pinned_blob_may_be_null: Where a provenance row gives a blob id, blob ids compare directly. Where it gives only a sha256, the tool digests `git cat-file blob <id>` and compares that. Both read the object store. A row that gives neither cannot be checked and would be a defect in this file.
how_to_read.what_this_file_is_not: It is not a second copy of fixtures/provenance.md and must not become one. It carries no byte counts, no retrieval narrative and no findings. If a digest here disagrees with fixtures/provenance.md, that file is right and this one is the defect.

kinds.git: A commit in a public repository. The tip is resolved with `git ls-remote`, and pinned paths are compared as blob ids or as sha256 over `git cat-file blob`.
kinds.http: A URL whose body is pinned by sha256. Checked with a GET.
kinds.ietf-draft: An Internet-Draft revision. Checked by probing whether revision NN+1 exists at the IETF archive.
kinds.local: A corpus THIS repository authors -- no upstream exists, so there is no tip, no URL and no revision to resolve. Checked for nothing but existence and digest: every path in `files` must be present and must still digest to the recorded sha256, read from the object store like every other comparison here. It reports `current` when they all do and `changed` when one does not, and it never touches the network. A `local` entry is not a claim that the bytes are correct -- only that they are still the bytes this file recorded.

how_to_read.corpus_dirs: Directories the entry's upstream produced WHOLE. A single pinned file is named by `pinned_file` and a `local` corpus by `files`, and neither is written as a directory: test/upstream-coverage.test.ts resolves every path under fixtures/ and refs/ through this file, and a `corpus_dirs` value broader than its upstream actually produced silently resolves paths that came from somewhere else. `refs` was such a value on all eleven single-file pins until 2026-09-06, and it made that test's own negative control resolve a draft nobody had pinned.
how_to_read.unmapped_rows: Each `unmapped` row carries an `id`, the `paths` it accounts for (globs; only `*` is special) and a one-line `reason`. The paths are what make the row machine-checkable: test/upstream-coverage.test.ts requires every path under fixtures/ and refs/, and every file of every corpus walker/scopes.json names, to resolve to an entry or to one of these rows, and requires every row to still account for something that exists.

unmapped_reason_codes._: A CLOSED vocabulary. Every `unmapped` row carries exactly one `reason_code` beside its prose `reason`, and test/upstream-coverage.test.ts fails on a row whose code is missing or is not one of the five below. The prose says why THIS row; the code says which KIND of absence it is, so an agent can decide what to do about it without parsing a sentence — which is the whole difference between a row a machine can act on and a row it can only display.
unmapped_reason_codes.generated_here: Produced in this repository — by a generator under tools/, or written by hand — so it is not a copy of any published artifact and has no upstream by construction. Nothing external can move.
unmapped_reason_codes.local_clone_no_remote: Copied from a git repository on this machine that has no remote: `git remote -v` prints nothing, so there is no ref whose tip could be resolved and none of the three fetchable kinds fits.
unmapped_reason_codes.nondeterministic_endpoint: A live endpoint whose body differs between two immediate requests — a fresh signature, a per-response nonce or timestamp. An `http` entry against it would report `changed` on every run forever, and a check that always fails says no more than one that cannot fail.
unmapped_reason_codes.past_capture: A record of a past event rather than a snapshot of something still being served: a signed capture, an emailed package. It has no tip, no URL and no revision, so no kind here can drift-check it, and re-fetching it is not a thing that can be done.
unmapped_reason_codes.repository_record: This repository's own bookkeeping about the corpora rather than corpus data. It was never fetched from anywhere and there is nothing upstream of it.

how_to_read.entry_check: B-151. An `http` entry may carry `check` at the ENTRY, because it pins one body and has no `paths` array. `fail` is the default and what an entry without the attribute means: a moved body is `changed` and reds the run. `note` still reports the move -- the outcome is still `changed`, both digests are printed, and the row is marked `(NOTE)` -- but it is counted in the SUMMARY's `noted=N` and does not red the run. It is for a pin that is MEANT to move. `note` never suppresses `unreachable`: a known mover that stops resolving is the upstream disappearing, not the upstream moving, and that has not passed. Every `note` requires a `check_reason_code` below.

check_reason_codes.author_bookkeeping: The upstream author's own record about their corpus rather than the corpus itself -- a manifest lock, a corpus_version, a licence or notice row. It moves whenever they touch any file in the directory, including files this repository does not pin.
check_reason_codes.rendered_page_furniture: The pinned bytes are a RENDERED page whose chrome moves independently of its content -- a per-deploy build id, a nav block, a footer date. The content this repository cites has not necessarily changed, and the digest cannot tell the two apart, so the pin cannot distinguish a real edit from a redeploy.
check_reason_codes.upstream_generated: Regenerated by the upstream's own tooling on a schedule or on every build, so a move carries no editorial decision.
check_reason_codes.mutable_pointer: The file's FUNCTION is to move: a registry pointer that names the current release, a status document carrying errata, a key file whose issuer has stated it will keep moving. Pinning it records what it said when we read it; failing on a move would fail it for doing its job. The move is still reported, and the value it moved to is still recorded, so a change of pointer is never lost -- only de-escalated.

unmapped.note: Paths under fixtures/, refs/, packages/ and registry/ that map to no upstream entry, each named, each carrying the paths it accounts for and a one-line reason, so the absence is a statement rather than an oversight. test/upstream-coverage.test.ts reads this block; nothing here is an exclusion the drift tool cannot see.
